newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 up but stagnation seen up to New Year.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 up but stagnation seen up to New Year.

text.p: The Czech PX50 closed 0.5 percent higher at 512.9 on Monday with three of the four most heavily capitalised issues on the index remaining unchanged.

While CEZ, Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna were all unmoved, SPT Telecom rose 16 crowns to 3,076. Dealers said the generally stagnant performance of the highly capitalised shares was likely to be repeated in the run-up to New Year.

"I would say that I don't expect any change from now till the beginning of January...I expect the market to be quite stable...At the moment there's no reason to rush into Czech equities," said Radim Bajgar of ING Barings.

Among the less heavily capitalised issues, most regional energy distributors posted moderate gains. Vychodoceska Energetika led the field with a 115 crown rise to 2,430. Two distributors, Prazska Energetika and Stredoceska Energeticka, lost ground.
Construction shares were mixed with IPS Praha gaining 11 crowns to 288 and Metrostav falling three crowns to 2,720.
The general dearth of interest in Czech equities was reflected in Monday's extremely low activity on the Prague Stock Exchange as a whole.
Turnover was just 329 million crowns with 577,396 shares traded.
